basics.name: Saiprapul Thotapally
basics.label: Senior Product Manager, AI
basics.summary: Senior Product Manager, AI at Global Payments who builds agentic platforms people trust, and has shipped them: a multi-agent system taken from concept to production in three months. Getting an agent to answer is the easy half; the product problem is earning enough confidence that a user lets it act. Owns the AI product strategy and roadmap for Genius, the autonomy and evaluation thresholds that decide when an agent may act, and the AI-first voice ordering thesis. Prices from measured product economics with GTM and commercialization. Researches agentic commerce and agent reputation.

work.name: Global Payments
work.summary: Senior PM for AI on Genius at Global Payments, and the product lead who took a multi-agent system from concept to production in three months. Owns the AI product strategy and roadmap, the funding case, the golden sets and evaluation gate that decide what reaches an operator, the voice ordering roadmap, and pricing and commercialization.
highlights: Took a multi-agent system from concept to production in 3 months by building golden sets per use case and making the regression run the release decision rather than a sign-off
In production it resolves 86% of operator questions directly across sales, labor, menu and payments in six languages, with 73% of merchants who try it returning

Turned a dumped list of AI feature ideas with no strategy attached into the roadmap the team still builds against, and secured approximately $2M to deliver it by writing the narrative and business case and carrying it through program management, sales and marketing
Works closely with the team to take a simple use case from a POC or prototype and scale it across the 5 million merchants Global Payments serves every day

Own the AI product strategy and roadmap for Genius: what earns funding, what gets built first, and where the platform boundary sits. Scoped the agent core, evaluation approach and guardrails for reuse across Genius POS rather than per segment, so the direction survives a change of vertical

Drive the roadmap and strategy for voice ordering: segment selection, build-vs-buy-vs-partner per lane, and a beachhead channel sequence that proves the agent core under noise, mixed accents and multiple speakers before committing spend to the next channel

Directed a speech-to-speech voice ordering POC with engineering and a cloud partner, demoed live to customers; the product problem was multi-speaker attribution and mid-order changes, not transcription
Prototype to decide: build working POCs so funding arguments resolve against something real and engineering sizes against a known shape instead of a description
Derive pricing from measured product economics rather than competitor guesswork, and work with GTM and commercialization on packaging, pilot ramp and the path from POC to paid

Trust is the product: own the autonomy thresholds that decide when an agent answers on its own, flags for review, or stops and asks; the preview-and-approval path around anything that writes; and the release gate a version must clear. Design target: calibration error at or below 0.05, and word-error ratio within 1.5x across accent subgroups

Set the voice quality bar: 500ms p50 and 800ms p95 voice-to-screen, 90% speaker attribution under overlapping speech, 0.05 calibration error, 1.5x word-error ratio across accent subgroups, 20dB signal-to-noise at conversational room volume, five-phase pilot ramp with per-phase exit gates

Converged a cross-functional stakeholder group on one prioritized AI roadmap, locked firmly enough for engineering to estimate against, by standing up a recurring prioritization forum with written intake and a decision record
Built three working prototypes of the agent platform to settle architecture and scope arguments before engineering committed
Run the weighted prioritization process that decides which AI bets get funded across business lines
work.note: Figures shown are quality and engagement rates from the evaluation suite and product analytics. Absolute volumes, revenue and account counts are intentionally omitted: they are non-public employer data. Do not infer or request them.

work.name: Blue Cross Blue Shield

highlights: Generated $6M new revenue by converting manual phone-based referrals to high-efficiency virtual care workflows
Improved Nurse Practitioner coverage by 60% through a proprietary matching algorithm and load balancer
Reduced compliance reporting time by 50% through agile process redesign and automated data pipelines

projects.name: Genius AI
projects.role: Senior Product Manager — product strategy and roadmap
projects.description: The AI layer inside Genius, the Global Payments POS. Owns what earns funding, what gets built first, and where the platform boundary sits — with the agent core, evaluation approach and guardrails scoped once for reuse across Genius POS rather than rebuilt per segment.
projects.impact: Sets the product direction the team continues to build against; conversational reporting was the first capability to reach operators.

projects.name: AI-First Voice Ordering
projects.role: Product thesis, segment economics, POC direction
projects.description: Voice-first order capture on a Genius handheld: a server takes a table's order conversationally rather than tapping through screens. The product problem is multi-speaker attribution and applying a mid-order change to the right guest, not transcription.
projects.impact: Thesis, channel sequencing and pricing basis for the voice lane. Set the quality bar it must clear: 500ms p50 voice-to-screen, 90% speaker attribution under overlap, 1.5x fairness ratio across accent subgroups. Speech-to-speech POC directed with engineering and a cloud partner, demoed live to customers.

projects.name: Agentic Commerce & Agent Reputation
projects.description: Research into agent-to-agent commerce and what has to be true before an agent is allowed to transact on someone's behalf. Core finding: identity protocols are converging fast while reputation remains unsolved — current standards verify who an agent is, not whether it honors terms or whether its past counterparties would deal with it again.
projects.impact: Reputation, not identity, is the gating layer for agent-initiated commerce, and the first credible reputation layer carries strong network effects. Same trust question as the day job, at network scale rather than one operator's.

projects.name: Aero Intelligence
projects.description: Side project: a multi-agent system bringing vision and voice to field technicians. Five LangGraph agents built on the Claude API automate technical document extraction and hands-free data entry.
projects.impact: Vision and voice capture that removes manual transcription from field reporting.

projects.name: AI Portfolio Prioritization Framework
projects.description: Weighted scoring methodology for evaluating enterprise AI investments across Internal Demand, Rinse & Repeat Potential, Customer Impact, Strategic Fit, and Feasibility.
projects.impact: Used to decide which enterprise AI bets get funded, and to defend saying no to low-impact ones.

projects.name: Complexity-Criticality Matrix for AI Governance
projects.description: Governance framework for determining AI oversight levels in compliance-heavy environments, published in IRJET 2024.
projects.impact: Used with Legal, Risk, Compliance and Security to set oversight levels for GenAI use cases.

projects.name: Consequence-Weighted AI Evaluation
projects.description: Evaluation methodology measuring AI systems by business impact of failure, not just standard accuracy metrics.
projects.impact: Reduced risk-adjusted delivery costs by identifying high-consequence edge cases early.

publications.title: How Processors Work: From Power to Program
publications.abstract: A museum-exhibit-style journey tracing how electricity becomes computation — from 0s and 1s through logic gates, binary adders and the ALU, up to how a CPU executes a program and how Python source ultimately runs on hardware.

publications.title: AI Evals Handbook
publications.abstract: A comprehensive guide to evaluating AI systems over time, focusing on Why, What, How, Keep, and Proof. Includes templates for RAG, agents, and drift monitoring.

publications.title: Complexity-Criticality Matrix for Enterprise GenAI Governance
publications.abstract: Governance framework for determining AI oversight levels, classifying tasks by domain specificity and compliance impact.

publications.title: Generative AI Unveiled: Mechanisms, Biases, and Ethical Engagement
publications.abstract: Technical deep-dive into LLM architecture, training dynamics, and frameworks for responsible deployment.

principles.title: Start with the user's blocker, not the technology
principles.description: I don't ask 'what can AI do?'—I ask 'what's stopping this user right now?' The best products dissolve constraints users didn't know they had.

principles.title: Prioritize ruthlessly, then earn the buy-in
principles.description: Strategy isn't what you build. It's what you don't build. I use weighted prioritization to defend the discipline of saying 'no' to low-impact AI bets.

principles.title: Build platforms, not projects
principles.description: Projects solve problems once. Platforms solve them forever. I architect for reusability across shared services for ingestion, orchestration, and guardrails.

principles.title: Measure what matters when AI fails
principles.description: I measure business impact of failure, weighting hallucinations by their consequence, and designing human-in-the-loop workflows that catch errors early.
